openings.claim: Future capability: a privately identified hold reports its current cart or shelf address, so the evening clerk retrieves it without surname shelving; delayed location reports cannot replace a newer address. This intervention is unproven. A presently testable enabling capability is rejecting obsolete movement reports.
openings.delta: Replace a once-daily exception assertion with per-book movement versions: only the greatest verified version supplies the address. Divider cards currently narrow surname search; the slip records exceptions, but neither supplied function establishes report freshness.
openings.prediction: In a paper simulation with deliberately delayed and duplicated movement reports, a version-aware ledger returns the stipulated latest address, even when the last report received names an older location.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is updating the exception slip more frequently and accepting the last received location. It performs equally with ordered reports but returns obsolete addresses when an older report arrives last.
openings.defeat: A correctly implemented version ledger selects an older stipulated location in the shuffled-report probe, or cannot complete the bounded probe within ten clerk-minutes. Ordered-report success alone would not establish the proposed enabling capability.
openings.probe: Have the existing clerk use paper, pencils and the timing sheet for a ten-minute closed-desk simulation of six anonymous holds moving among the existing cart and shelves. Each scripted move has a fixed increasing book-specific version; shuffle delivery and repeat older reports. Compare version-aware and last-received ledgers against the scripted final positions, recording wrong answers and time. No reader handoffs occur.
assumptions: Fit evaluates only this bounded paper probe; it neither proves live retrieval nor the 95-percent pickup target.

A future deployment requires reliable opaque book identifiers, movement detection, private identity lookup, trusted movement sequencing and the existing clerk's reader verification; their availability is unconfirmed.
Every real move must generate an accurate report; versions cannot repair undetected movement or a report attached to the wrong book.
Live capture, lookup and daily preparation must be demonstrated within staffing, privacy, furniture and ten-minute constraints.
